title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with cream sauce and added vegetables is a restaurant (3667) dish made from whole‑grain pasta, a smooth cream sauce, and fresh vegetables. The whole‑grain pasta retains bran and germ, making it more nutritious, while the cream sauce gives the dish a velvety texture and mild flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta provides more fiber and micronutrients than regular white pasta.
The cream sauce is often made with a blend of cream and low‑fat milk to reduce calories in restaurant (3667).
Vegetables may include broccoli, spinach, bell pepper, and zucchini, boosting vitamin and antioxidant content.
The dish is served hot, frequently topped with grated Parmesan or oregano for extra aroma.
Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains soluble and insoluble fiber that supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and potassium, while the pasta contributes iron and magnesium.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Because of the whole grain, the dish raises blood glucose more slowly, which is beneficial for weight management and diabetes control.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: The cream sauce, prepared with a touch of olive oil, provides monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Broccoli, spinach, and bell pepper contain carotenoids and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cream sauce may contain dairy, which can cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The creamy sauce adds significant calories; portion control is advisable for those watching weight.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt in the sauce can increase sodium intake; individuals with hypertension should ask for reduced salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossing it with the sauce and vegetables. Garnish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan, or nuts for extra texture. It can be paired with a light mixed‑green salad if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or milk to keep the sauce from becoming too thick.
